title: Frontend state management Redux Toolkit and MobX comparisons
concepts: Choose state ownership by the lifetime and consumers of the data: component-local UI state, URL state, server cache, and cross-feature client state solve different problems.
React local state and Context are built in. Redux Toolkit adds an explicit store and action-driven transitions; MobX tracks observable reads and propagates updates through a dynamic dependency graph.

Server data has fetching, caching, invalidation, and synchronization requirements that differ from client-owned UI state. RTK Query is an optional data-fetching and caching system integrated with Redux Toolkit.
Avoid putting all application data into one global store. Select the smallest appropriate boundary and keep derived values derived instead of duplicating them.
Redux favors explicit, serializable transitions and inspectable action histories. MobX favors mutable observable models, computed derivations, and automatic dependency tracking.
No state tool removes the need for clear ownership, data normalization, predictable updates, error handling, testing, and measured performance.

2.13 moved package build tooling to TSDown/PNPM and added official TypeScript 7 support; public package layout/exports and APIs were unchanged from 2.12.
2.14 added dispatch and RTK Query type-checking performance improvements, cache-entry selectors, a DevTools action sanitizer, and other fixes.

MobX 7 removes the Proxy-less ES5 fallback and MobX 6 legacy decorator mode. Projects using legacy decorators must migrate to modern decorators or another annotation style; environments without Proxy support should remain on MobX 6.
